concerns.text: The plan fits a VAR/VECM on only two macro variables (GDP, Unemployment) plus sentiment, despite the specification (FR‑002) also requiring consumer confidence. Omitting this variable can introduce omitted‑variable bias, threatening the validity of causal inference.

Out‑of‑sample validation is performed by masking recession periods and re‑fitting the model. This does not constitute a true predictive hold‑out (no forward‑looking test) and may overstate robustness; a proper train‑test split or rolling‑origin forecast should be used.

Linear interpolation is used for missing macro values (≤5 % missing). Interpolation can induce artificial autocorrelation, especially in short quarterly series (~120 observations), potentially biasing VAR lag selection and Granger tests. The plan should assess interpolation impact or consider model‑based imputation.

Stationarity testing relies on ADF with a maximum lag of 12 quarters. With limited sample size, high lag orders reduce test power and may lead to over‑differencing; a more conservative lag selection (e.g., based on information criteria) is advisable.

The sensitivity analysis threshold (absolute p‑value shift ≤ 0.02) is arbitrary and not justified by a power analysis. Given the modest sample size, even small shifts may be statistically meaningful; the plan should link the threshold to a formal power calculation or effect‑size criterion.
